name: Bard on the Beach Volunteer Program
org: Bard on the Beach Shakespeare Festival
what_you_do: Work at the front of the theater as a greeter, ticket taker or usher. You can also help in the shop or snack bar, or at events at the Vanier Park festival.
deadline_text: Applications are closed until early 2027.

name: Canadian Cadets (Sea, Army and Air Cadets)
org: Department of National Defence (Government of Canada)
city: Local corps and squadrons across British Columbia
what_you_do: Join a local Sea, Army or Air Cadet corps or squadron. It is a national youth program with challenging activities and training. You pick the cadet element that interests you.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Register online and the unit staff contact you.

name: Foundry Work & Education Program (FWEP)
what_you_do: Get personalized one-on-one support to explore and reach your work and education goals. Help includes resumes, interviewing and managing stress. It is a support program, not a paid job.
deadline_text: No dates. Foundry says no referral is needed to use its services.

name: SkilledTradesBC Youth Trades Programs (Discover, Explore, Train and Work in Trades)
org: SkilledTradesBC, with the Ministry of Education and Child Care
city: Across British Columbia (through your high school)
what_you_do: Start a trade while you are still in high school. Train in Trades means trades classes and one level of technical training. Work in Trades means paid on-the-job training while you attend high school.
grades: High school students (grade and age rules are not stated on the program pages)
deadline_text: No application deadline is stated on the program pages. Talk to your school for dates.

name: Skills Canada BC Competitions (regionals and provincials)
city: Regional events around British Columbia, provincials in Abbotsford
what_you_do: Compete with other students. Pick a trade or tech skill, such as animation or robotics. The site lists contests. They are regional, provincial and national.
grades: Jr. Skills Projects are for grades 6 to 9. Other competitions are labelled Sec. (secondary) or PS (post-secondary).
deadline_text: Regionals run February to March 2027 in communities around the province, exact dates not posted yet. Provincials: April 14, 2027 at Abbotsford Tradex. Nationals: May 27 and 28, 2027 in Calgary. Registration deadlines are not listed.

name: Burien Green Teens
what_you_do: Two weeks of restoring Salmon Creek Ravine while exploring green careers and earning a stipend. No experience needed. Gloves, tools and lunch are provided.
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran May 25 to June 25, 2026. Next year not posted.

name: Volunteer Program at Burnaby Hospital
what_you_do: Help patients and visitors at Burnaby Hospital. You might give directions, eat meals with patients, visit them, or help in clinics. Open spots vary by area.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. The page says some areas may have no openings.

name: Become a Lifeguard and Swim Instructor
org: City of Burnaby Parks, Recreation and Culture
what_you_do: Take Lifesaving Society courses with the City. They are Bronze Medallion, Bronze Cross, First Aid, then pool lifeguard and swim teacher. They prepare you to work at Burnaby pools.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Register for courses online or at a pool front desk.

name: Burnaby Village Museum Volunteer Program
org: City of Burnaby, Burnaby Village Museum
what_you_do: Greet visitors in old time clothes. Help with school programs and special events, work with old objects, or help at camps. The museum is a 10 acre village from the past.
deadline_text: Intakes: February (spring/summer) and September (fall/winter) for costumed interpretation, school programs and events. Camps: February and April. Collections and sewing: ongoing.

name: Camp Ignite
org: Camp Ignite Society (with Metro Vancouver fire departments)
what_you_do: A firefighting camp for young women. Real firefighters are your mentors. Learn to cut people from cars, handle dangerous spills, rope rescue, first aid, fitness and teamwork.
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed. 2026 camp was Aug 7 to 9. Next year not posted.

name: Job Corps (Cascades, Curlew and Columbia Basin centers, Washington)
org: U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps
city: Sedro-Woolley, Curlew and Moses Lake, WA
what_you_do: Free live-on-campus career training. Centers list computer and medical assistant, carpentry, cement masonry, human services, fire management and nursing assistant training.
deadline_text: Open enrollment: you can start the application at any time.

name: King County Library System Teen Advisory Boards
city: King County, WA (branches outside the city of Seattle)
what_you_do: Teen volunteers meet with a librarian. They give input on library services. They help design library programs and events.
deadline_text: No deadline. The page lists upcoming meetings (for example Maple Valley, Lake Forest Park, Newport Way and Federal Way); contact the local library to join.

name: Lynn Canyon Ecology Centre Volunteer
org: District of North Vancouver, Lynn Canyon Ecology Centre
what_you_do: Help keep Lynn Canyon Park clean (age 10+) or provide support during the spring and summer mini-camps for kids (age 13+).
deadline_text: The page says 2026 summer mini-camps are at capacity for volunteers. It says applications get a reply within 10 business days. No ongoing-acceptance statement.

name: Teen Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Volunteer with the City Library's teen program. The page does not describe the roles.
deadline_text: Registration for January 2027 opportunities opens Dec. 17 at 5 p.m., per the library's teen hub page (year inferred). Fall 2026 registration is closed.

name: Become a Lifeguard and Swim Instructor at NVRC
org: North Vancouver Recreation and Culture Commission
what_you_do: Take the courses in order. They are Bronze Medallion, Bronze Cross, First Aid, National Lifeguard Pool and Swim Instructor. Then apply online for pool jobs with NVRC.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

name: Volunteer with North Vancouver Recreation and Culture (NVRC)
org: North Vancouver Recreation and Culture Commission
what_you_do: Help with swimming, young kids programs, fitness and special events. You can also help with general recreation.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

name: Youth Train in Trades (North Vancouver School District)
org: North Vancouver School District 44 with BCIT, VCC and SkilledTradesBC
what_you_do: Take a trades training program while in high school. Training is at a high school, partner college or certified facility. Seats are limited.
deadline_text: Deadline is the end of February for programs the next school year. Year not stated.

name: GRuB Summer Youth Program
what_you_do: Work and learn on the GRuB Farm: planting, harvesting, irrigation, composting, the market stand and bouquet CSA. Add leadership workshops, field trips and weekly group meals.
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications are full and closed. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Teen Ambassadors
what_you_do: Team up with other teens and library staff to plan programs and help choose teen books.
deadline_text: Closed as of 2026-10-10. The program page says registration is currently full. No next intake date is posted.

name: Richmond RCMP Youth Academy
org: Richmond RCMP and Richmond School District 38
what_you_do: A one-week summer day camp. You learn about police duties, the legal system, criminal justice, fitness and teamwork.
deadline_text: 6th academy is planned for August 2027. Applications posted late 2026 to early 2027. Due April 6, 2027.

name: Biomedical and Health Sciences Dual Credit (Richmond SD38 with KPU)
org: Richmond School District 38 and Kwantlen Polytechnic University
what_you_do: Take four college level health science courses full time at KPU Surrey from February to June of Grade 12. You earn high school and university credit.
deadline_text: Application form posted fall 2026. Due March 9, 2027 for the 2027-28 school year.

name: Business Dual Credit (Richmond SD38 with KPU Melville School of Business)
org: Richmond School District 38 and Kwantlen Polytechnic University
what_you_do: Take four business courses that transfer to a university. They are marketing, talking at work, how groups work, and accounting. You go full time at KPU Surrey in semester 2.
deadline_text: Applications for 2027-28 are available. Due date not found on the program page. The page says applications are due the year before.

name: Youth TRAIN in Trades (Richmond SD38)
what_you_do: Start Level 1 trades training at a college while still in high school. You earn high school and college credit. You are signed up as an apprentice with SkilledTradesBC.
deadline_text: Applications for 2027-28 are open. Preferred deadline Feb 2, 2027. Second deadline Mar 2, 2027.

name: Youth WORK in Trades (Richmond SD38)
what_you_do: Get paid work in a SkilledTradesBC trade and earn high school credit for it. Your work hours count toward an apprenticeship.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

name: Youth Civic Engagement Program
what_you_do: Learn how City departments work and how decisions get made. Teams build a project and present it to a mock City Council.
deadline_text: 2026 session was July 7 to 9, 2026. Next dates not posted.

name: Richmond Youth Media Program (RYMP)
what_you_do: A free media lab with drop in times and skill sessions. You can learn animation, digital drawing and film editing. Later you can use your skills on real jobs like event photos and DJing.
deadline_text: No deadline. Drop-ins: Tue 4-6pm, Thu 4-6pm, Sat 12-4pm.

name: ANEW Construction Trades Training (teens with disabilities)
city: Washington (site not stated on the page)
what_you_do: A 40 hour paid training in building jobs for students with disabilities. ANEW runs it with a state job help office. Students earn a certificate.
deadline_text: Summer 2026 applications are closed. The 2026 application deadline was April 30, with notice in early June. No 2027 dates are posted.

grades: 9 to 12 (high school, Running Start, GED or homeschool)
name: Youth Ocean Advocates
what_you_do: Teen volunteers teach visitors about marine life and ocean protection. They join projects like beach cleanups and community science. They get behind-the-scenes tours. They get about 20 hours of training.
deadline_text: School Year 2026-27 Currents interest form is closed. The page says to check back in February 2027 for the Summer 2027 interest form (its general timeline says January; confirm with the Aquarium). Info sessions run over Zoom in March (summer) and September (school year).

name: YouthForce Teen Jobs
org: Boys & Girls Clubs of King County
what_you_do: Teens get job skills workshops on resumes, interviews and money. Then they get paid internships with local employers. TeamWork Internships are paid game day jobs at Mariners, Kraken and Seahawks games.
deadline_text: No dates posted. The page has an Apply button for TeamWork internships and a resume help form.

name: Voices in Science: Burke-ology (high school)
what_you_do: Free sessions where high school students study one science, such as ancient plants or fish. Teens tour behind the scenes at the Burke collections. They speak at a public STEAM Spotlight Symposium.
deadline_text: Applications for the spring 2026 session are closed. Future dates are not posted; the Burke asks teens to join its Youth and Family Programs e-newsletter.

name: Seattle Children's Hospital Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Weekly volunteer shifts at the hospital and regional clinics. Roles vary; see the position summaries on the volunteer site.
deadline_text: The volunteer portal says applications open each March, July and November and stay open until positions are filled. None of those windows is open as of Oct 11; the next one is November.

name: Research Training Program for High School Students
what_you_do: Four weeks of hands-on biology lab training in downtown Seattle. Teens learn lab skills like PCR and gene editing. They join workshops on college and careers. They present a project of their own.
deadline_text: The 2026 application closed March 8, 2026 (letters due March 29). The page says to check back in late 2026 for summer 2027.

name: Youth Voice Research Liaison Program
what_you_do: Paid training in how research works, then teens consult with Seattle Children's research teams. They give feedback on study plans and outreach and help share results in youth-friendly ways.
deadline_text: No application cycle for 2026-27. The next cycle is 2027-28 and dates are not posted. (The 2025-26 deadline was Sept 1, 2025.)

name: Clean Water Ambassadors Internship
org: Mountains to Sound Greenway Trust with King County Wastewater Treatment Division
what_you_do: Learn about clean water, teach students, interview people who work in environmental jobs, and give a final presentation. Field trips and workshops are part of it.
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran April 1 to 22, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Seattle Fire Cadet Program (Company 511)
what_you_do: Train on Saturdays at the fire department training facility to learn what firefighting is like. You get a helmet, coat, pants, boots and gloves for training.
deadline_text: Applications accepted all year. Apply Feb 1 to July 31 and hear back in August. Apply Aug 1 to Jan 31 and hear back in February.

grades: Entering senior year (the page also says 'between 11th and 12th grade')
name: Fred Hutch Summer High School Internship Program (SHIP)
what_you_do: This is eight weeks of paid, full-time lab work. The first two weeks teach lab safety and technique. Then you spend six weeks in a Fred Hutch research group. You go to seminars and college and career workshops. You end with a presentation.
deadline_text: 2026 applications are closed. The page says information on the 2027 program will be posted in November 2026.

name: YESS Restoration Ecology Internship (Riverview and WANIC)
org: Mountains to Sound Greenway Trust, Riverview School District and WANIC Skill Center
city: Carnation, WA and field sites in King County
what_you_do: Work outdoors on projects that heal land across King County. Take a summer Restoration Ecology course. Build skills in plant ID and public speaking. Give a talk on your final project.
grades: Rising 9th to 12th graders (rising 12th graders get first priority)
deadline_text: 2026 applications ran March 24 to April 23, 2026 on the WANIC summer course site. Next year not posted.

name: Henry Teen Art Collective
what_you_do: A weekly group of teens. They go behind the scenes at the museum and meet artists and creative workers. They make projects like zines, art shows and videos.
deadline_text: The newest date on the page is old. The only call for applications listed is for 2023-24, with a deadline of October 10, 2023. No newer call is posted. Ask the museum if a new call is open.

name: History Lab
what_you_do: A two week summer program at the history museum. Teens learn how to research and tell local history. Then they publish their own project on the Rainy Day History website.
deadline_text: 2026 deadline was May 22, 2026 and has passed. The page says to check back in spring 2027.

name: Youth Volunteer (ages 16 to 17)
what_you_do: Teen volunteers help visitors at the air and space museum. Roles include guiding tours, helping with school trips, and acting out history with costumes and props. Open roles are listed on the page.
deadline_text: Roles are recruited by season. No single deadline. Browse current roles and apply online.

name: Career Explorations (Mentorship and Internship)
what_you_do: Teens do a 4 Saturday job training and mentor program. Then they can apply for a paid summer internship with Seattle Parks. Interns work 20 hours a week for 8 weeks, for example on summer meals and playgrounds.
deadline_text: Page says mentorship applications opened in August 2026. Mentorship starts the first Saturday of October, November, February, March and April. No close date stated.

name: Seattle Parks and Recreation Lifeguard
what_you_do: You watch swimmers. You respond to emergencies. You help teach swim skills. This is at city swim beaches and indoor and outdoor pools.
deadline_text: The last posting closed June 16, 2026. The Aquatics page says Temporary/Intermittent Lifeguards are hired year-round, even when no posting is active.

name: Seattle Parks Summer Temporary Jobs
what_you_do: Work a city summer job such as wading pool attendant, aquatics customer service, boat ramp ranger or lifeguard. Some jobs are mostly weekends and some include first aid training.
deadline_text: 2026 postings closed between May 12 and June 16, 2026 (page updated April 14, 2026). 2027 postings not posted.

name: Teen Late Night Internship
what_you_do: Interns help run Late Night teen events at Seattle teen life centers and community centers. They check teens in. They help with games, contests, community dinners and service projects.
deadline_text: Applications for the January to June cohort open in December. Applications for the June to December cohort open in May. Exact close dates are not stated.

name: Teen Summer Musical
what_you_do: A summer theater program where youth rehearse and perform a full musical (Peter Pan in 2026). The program is aimed at youth of color. Rehearsals ran June 29 to Aug 27 in 2026, with shows Aug 28 to 30.
deadline_text: 2026 auditions were April 17 and 18. 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Seattle Parks Youth Employment and Service Learning: Pre-Employment Training
what_you_do: A 7-week, 14-hour after-school job readiness class (resume writing, time management, professional communication) at Teen Life Centers or community centers. Finishing it unlocks Parks paid internships.
deadline_text: Offered each Fall, Winter and Spring quarter. The page does not list current dates, so email to ask.

name: Seattle Police Explorers
what_you_do: Learn how police work through monthly meetings and visits to units like K-9 and Harbor Patrol. Volunteer at community events, such as directing traffic and security work. Uniforms are provided.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Explorers meet monthly.

name: PV Events Fellowship
what_you_do: Lead the planning of Girlvolution, a youth arts and social justice event, with training, a mentor and a $5,000 event budget. Also help run 3 other community events.
deadline_text: Applications closed for 2026. The page says to check back next year. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Healing Justice Fellowship
what_you_do: Support peers, help build a healing justice curriculum and help plan the Healing Justice Summit. You work with a team of staff, mental health providers and community partners.
deadline_text: Applications closed for 2026. The page says to check back next year. 2027 dates not posted.

name: Junior Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Volunteer in a hospital with training for your role. You do about 48 hours over roughly 3 months with at least one 3 to 4 hour shift a week.
deadline_text: No application dates are listed. The page says to apply through the online form.

name: Puget Sound Skills Center
org: Puget Sound Skills Center (Highline Public Schools)
what_you_do: Spend half your school day in a hands-on career class such as aerospace manufacturing, dental assisting, certified nursing assistant, video game programming, auto, construction or cyber security. 21 programs.
deadline_text: The 2026-27 lottery has run and all offers have been made. The admissions page asks students still interested in 2026-27 to complete the PSSC Application interest form. The 2027-28 window is not posted.

name: Summer Youth Employment Program
city: Seattle, WA (serves SW and SE Seattle and South King County)
what_you_do: A 6-week paid summer internship for 20 teens. Interns explore career paths, take field trips, hear guest speakers and work on personal growth.
grades: Entering 9th grade (fall 2026) through high school seniors (Class of 2030)
deadline_text: 2026 applications opened in April 2026. Close date not stated. 2027 dates not posted.

name: SCA Seattle High School Conservation Crews (Urban Green)
what_you_do: Work on a crew led by two adult Crew Leaders. You do parks and nature projects. There are field trips to learn about the earth across western Washington.
deadline_text: Not posted; the page is about a past season, call to ask.

name: SDOT Youth Ambassador Program
what_you_do: Visit transportation sites, meet people in planning, engineering and communications, job shadow, and build resume and interview skills. Learn about advocacy for fair transportation.
deadline_text: 2026 applications closed June 16, 2026. Program ran Aug 4 to 27, 2026. 2027 dates not posted.

grades: Enrolled in high school (classes of 2027 to 2030)
name: TIPS Summer Internship
what_you_do: Work part time at a local nonprofit for the summer. TIPS hires you and places you based on your interests, such as a camp, an arts group or a food bank.
deadline_text: Applications open mid to late November 2026 (exact day not posted). Deadline Feb 5, 2027. Interviews early to mid March, decisions April 2027.

name: The New Guard (teen arts leaders)
what_you_do: A cohort of teens works with TeenTix and Seattle arts groups. They learn about arts careers, give feedback from the teen view, lead skill-shares and act as a teen council.
deadline_text: TeenTix's Program Applications page says: Applications for 2026/27 programs are now closed! Applications for the 2027-2028 program year will open in Spring 2027.

name: TeenTix Newsroom
what_you_do: Teen writers see arts events for free and write reviews that are edited by teen editors and posted on the TeenTix blog. Some work is also shared with Encore and The Seattle Times.
deadline_text: TeenTix's Program Applications page says: Applications for 2026/27 programs are now closed! Applications for the 2027-2028 program year will open in Spring 2027.

name: Rainier Beach Youth Stewards
what_you_do: Work at the Rainier Beach Urban Farm and Wetlands. You help heal the wetland and teach about the farm. You also do team building, field trips and workshops.
deadline_text: Dates and deadline not posted on the page. Applicants are encouraged to apply for all seasons.

grades: Washington high school students in 10th or 11th grade when applying (rising juniors and seniors)
name: Changemakers in Computing
org: University of Washington Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science & Engineering
what_you_do: This in-person summer program runs four weeks at UW Seattle. You learn coding through projects. You explore how technology affects society. You work in groups led by UW undergraduate mentors.
deadline_text: 2026 cohort: applications opened March 4 and closed April 1, 2026 (11:59pm PT); decisions April 27; orientation May 16. 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Engineering Academy
org: University of Washington College of Engineering
what_you_do: A free one week summer program at UW Seattle for teens new to engineering. Students do hands-on design tasks, meet engineering students and teachers, and tour campus.
grades: 10 or 11 (during the school year before the summer)
deadline_text: The 2026 application is closed. The page says the 2027 application will open in March.

name: Business and Leadership Program (UW Foster School of Business)
org: University of Washington Foster School of Business with Summer Springboard
what_you_do: This is a two-week summer program on the UW Seattle campus. It has leadership workshops. You join a real-world business case competition. You visit two Seattle companies.
deadline_text: No application window posted. The only session listed was July 5 to 17, 2026 (has passed). 2027 dates are not posted; 'spaces are limited.'

name: UW Nurse Camp
org: University of Washington School of Nursing
what_you_do: A week long day camp. You shadow nurses at two UW hospitals, learn CPR and how to take vital signs, practice in simulation labs and meet nurses from different fields.
deadline_text: 2026 camp ran July 20 to 24, 2026. Applications for 2027 open February 15, 2027. Closing date not stated.

name: UW Summer Sessions for High School Students
what_you_do: High school students take regular UW summer courses for college credit. More than 1,000 courses are offered on campus and online.
deadline_text: The page gives 2026 steps (eighth grade completed by June 30, 2026; summer began June 22, 2026). Its calendar lists February 2027 as when the Time Schedule and application open for 2027, with no exact date.

grades: Grades 11 and 12 for full-year classes. Summer semester: students entering grades 9 to 12.
name: WANIC Skill Center (career and technical classes)
org: Washington Network for Innovative Careers (WANIC), Lake Washington School District
what_you_do: Take tuition-free, year-long career classes in three-period blocks while still in high school. Many give high school and college credit or an industry certification. A summer semester is also offered.
deadline_text: The full-year priority window ran Feb 4, 2026 to March 31, 2026. Full-year applications closed July 15 (the year is not printed on that line). Summer 2027 information is not posted yet.

name: YouthCAN
what_you_do: A free after-school arts program. Teens work with teaching artists on art about identity and culture, learn about arts careers, and show their work in the museum's youth gallery.
deadline_text: No dates posted. The page says registration typically opens in the spring and is first come, first served. Email the museum to ask about info sessions.

grades: Entering 10th to 12th grade in the fall of the program year (2026 page)
name: Woodland Park Zoo Teen Ambassador Volunteer Program
what_you_do: You meet each week to learn about conservation careers, public speaking and teamwork. You also pick your own volunteer shifts at the zoo. There are 20 shifts. They can include Zoomazium, new habitats and animal behavior observation.
deadline_text: 2026 cohort: application deadline Friday, March 27, 2026, 5:00 pm; Q&A sessions in March; interviews mid-April; decisions early May. 2027 dates are not posted.

grades: Grades 6 to 12 for monthly service projects
name: YMCA Earth Service Corps
what_you_do: Join a youth-led environmental club at your school or start one. Take part in monthly service projects, a leaders summit, spring retreats and a spring environmental symposium.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Events: Environmental Leaders Summit (the page says both winter and each fall), Eco-Retreats and Environmental Symposium (spring).

name: Summer Day Camp Staff
what_you_do: Be a role model and lead campers in grades 1 to 8 through crafts, STEM, archery, hikes and outdoor games at a local YMCA summer day camp.
deadline_text: Page says "Now hiring for summer". No application window posted for summer 2027. Training for some jobs starts in May or June.

name: WAGES Ten Week Internship Program
org: YMCA of Greater Seattle Social Impact Center
what_you_do: Explore a career path and get paid to learn job and life skills. The program is run with Thompson Hotels and Machinists INC and funded by the City of Seattle.
deadline_text: No dates posted. The page appears out of date (it mentions a 2025 event), so ask about the next cohort.

name: Youth and Government (Youth Legislature)
what_you_do: Join a weekly delegation, write your own bill, then debate and vote on student bills as a mock legislator at the State Capitol conference in Olympia.
deadline_text: Fill out the interest form before your branch's first meeting. Delegations start meeting Oct 19 to Oct 22, 2026 (Bellevue Oct 20, Coal Creek Oct 19, Dale Turner Oct 22, East Madison Oct 21, Northshore Oct 21, Snoqualmie Valley Oct 22), and Sammamish starts Nov 4. A free open house is Wednesday, Oct 14, 6:00 to 7:30 pm at the East Madison YMCA, no RSVP. The Oct 8 open house has passed. No sign-up deadline is stated.

name: Seattle Youth Commission
what_you_do: Fifteen teens are picked by the Mayor and City Council. They advise the City on rules that affect youth. They plan a community project and a yearly event. They learn public speaking and how to organize.
deadline_text: Applications are paused. Email the commission to be told when it reopens. No dates posted.

name: Seattle Youth Employment Program (SYEP)
org: City of Seattle Human Services Department
what_you_do: These are paid summer internships. They are in City departments, local businesses and nonprofits. They run July 6 to Aug 18 in 2026. There is also a school-year Learn & Earn job skills program with stipends.
deadline_text: 2026 internship applications ran March 18 to May 5, 2026 (closed). Learn & Earn Foundations 2026-27 applications ran Aug 11 to Sept 25, 2026 (closed). 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Creative Career Cohort
what_you_do: Learn photography and design, work on real projects for paying clients, build a portfolio and practice job interviews. Meets twice a week at the Youth in Focus office.
deadline_text: 2027 application "opens soon". Exact dates are not set on the page. The page lists the 2027 steps as a November deadline (a Sunday, date not set), interviews in December and a January start.

name: Job Training Program (Photography)
what_you_do: Get paid to photograph events for local groups and businesses, with a teaching artist mentoring you. Youth in Focus provides all the camera equipment.
deadline_text: No deadline. Take a class first, then ask about jobs.

name: Day Camp and Youth Service Volunteer
org: City of Surrey Parks, Recreation and Culture
what_you_do: Help staff run sport, art, dance, drama, science and themed day camps and youth programs at Surrey rec centres.
deadline_text: Not stated on the program page. Check for the next intake.

name: Surrey Leadership Youth Council (SLYC)
what_you_do: Twenty Surrey teens meet every other week at City Hall. They give the city a youth voice. They plan the Youth Speak Up Forum and the Surrey Leadership Action Conference.
deadline_text: Applications for this term are closed. The city says they reopen in Spring 2027.

name: Reading Buddies (Teen Big Buddies)
what_you_do: Read with a child in grades 2 to 4 for one hour a week for six weeks and do fun reading activities. You are the 'Big Buddy'.
deadline_text: Fall 2026 teen applications closed. Fall sessions run Oct 13 to Nov 25, 2026. Spring sessions are expected next.

name: Teen Library Council
what_you_do: Teen ambassadors for the library plan events. They tell the library what services teens want. Six councils meet at branches around Surrey.
deadline_text: Applications are closed. The page gives no reopening date.

name: Volunteer Program at Surrey Memorial Hospital
what_you_do: Help with information, giving directions and office tasks. You also support patients. Some units need volunteers who are 20 or older.
deadline_text: No deadline stated. Applications are kept on file for four months.

name: YEP Projects (Youth Engagement Proposal)
what_you_do: Pitch a youth-led project for Surrey, like an event, public art or a workshop. Funding may be available but is not guaranteed.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

name: Youth Event Squad (YES)
what_you_do: Work with city staff to plan youth events like Surrey Slam Jam, the Youth Cooking Showdown and the Kids Conference. You also help run them on the day.
deadline_text: Applications for this term are closed. The city says they reopen in Spring 2027.

name: Surrey Youth Stewardship Squad (SYSS)
what_you_do: Drop-in park work with other teens: pull invasive plants, plant trees and shrubs, clean up litter and improve habitat. Tools and training are provided.
deadline_text: Drop-in dates: Sep 25, Oct 23 and Nov 14, 2026. More dates go to registered members.

name: Teen Councils
what_you_do: Drop-in teen groups that plan library programs, give feedback and do service projects. Teens earn volunteer hours and build leadership skills. There is also a virtual council.
deadline_text: Runs October through April. No application, so you can join any time during the season.

name: Teen Volunteer League
what_you_do: A six-week summer service-learning program. A cohort of teens meets weekly and works on service projects to build resume skills.
deadline_text: Applications typically open in April and are posted on the teen volunteering page. 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Jobs 253 Internships
what_you_do: Internships with Tacoma businesses and groups. Students apply in SchooLinks and interview with employers. They finish their hours and tasks. They earn school credit and a stipend.
deadline_text: The page lists the 2026-27 sessions: Session 1 Sept 9 to Nov 19 (applications open in August); Session 2 Nov 30 to Feb 4 (applications open in October); Session 3 Feb 17 to Apr 15 (January); Session 4 Apr 26 to June 17 (March); Session 5 July 6 to Aug 20 (May). It gives only the month each window opens, not exact dates, and does not say whether Session 2 applications are open today. Check SchooLinks.

name: Jobs 253 Summer Credential Programs
what_you_do: Free summer training from experts. The 2026 page lists courses in cars, cooking, digital drawing, business starts, plumbing, building, drones and wildland fire. Students earn credentials.
deadline_text: The auto course priority deadline was April 30. 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Art Exchange (Vancouver Art Gallery and Arts Umbrella)
org: Vancouver Art Gallery with Arts Umbrella
what_you_do: This is a year-long visual arts program for young teens. You visit the Vancouver Art Gallery behind the scenes. You also take workshops there. Then you do studio projects at Arts Umbrella on Granville Island.
deadline_text: Submissions for the 2026-27 program were due Tuesday, September 29, 2026 at 8 AM. Next cycle not posted.

grades: Aged 15 to 18 or entering Grades 10, 11 or 12 in fall 2026
name: Teen Art Group (Vancouver Art Gallery and Emily Carr University)
org: Vancouver Art Gallery with Emily Carr University of Art + Design
what_you_do: This is a weekly arts program. It moves between the Vancouver Art Gallery and Emily Carr University studios. At the Gallery, you hear talks from curators and artists. You build a portfolio.
deadline_text: Registration for fall 2026 is open as of Oct 10, 2026, with no closing date stated. The program starts Oct 15, 2026. The scholarship deadline was September 15, 2026.

name: Mini Med School: Inside the Human Body (BC Children's Hospital Research Institute)
what_you_do: You attend four evening sessions. They cover recent advances in health and medical research. You can go in person in Vancouver or online. If you attend all four, you can apply for a $1,000 CAD tuition scholarship.
deadline_text: 2026 sessions are Nov 5, 12, 19 and 26, 2026. Registration for 2026 is closed and the waitlist is full. A new round is not posted yet.

name: Pathways to Science (BC Children's Hospital Research Institute)
what_you_do: Join free online talks from researchers and health professionals about science and health careers. It is lecture style. Cameras and microphones stay off and you ask questions in the chat.
deadline_text: Ten Monday sessions from Sept 2026 to June 2027 (Sept 21, 2026 is 6 to 7 p.m.; the others are 5 to 6 p.m.). No deadline is posted. You can sign up any time during the series until 1,000 students have applied.

name: Youth Employability Program (BGC South Coast BC)
what_you_do: This is an 8-week program. About four weeks are job skills workshops and certificate training. Certificates include First Aid, WHMIS, Superhost and Serving It Right. Then you get up to four weeks of paid work experience with a local employer.
deadline_text: Sessions run every other month (the page gives Oct, Dec, Feb, Apr as examples) and recruiting starts one month before each start date. No events were listed when read.

name: Discovery Days in Health Sciences (BC Children's Hospital)
org: Canadian Medical Hall of Fame with BC Children's Hospital Research Institute
what_you_do: Spend one day at BC Children's Hospital Research Institute. You learn about careers in medicine, health science and research.
deadline_text: Friday, Nov 6, 2026. No student deadline is posted. Student sign-up opens about six weeks before event day (around late September 2026). School registration for fall events opens in Sept 2026, and student sign-up instructions are emailed to the contact teacher when registration opens.

grades: Grades 11 and 12 for the High School Work Experience placement
name: Science World Volunteer Program
what_you_do: Volunteers support the science centre. You work a weekly 2 to 3 hour shift. You get training and recognition. Lower Mainland Grade 11 and 12 students can also do a High School Work Experience placement.
deadline_text: The core volunteer intake is closed; intake and training sessions are scheduled each year. No dates posted.

name: seed2STEM Summer Research Internship
org: ICORD, University of British Columbia (with SFU and Kelowna sites)
what_you_do: Indigenous high school students work in a university research lab on a STEM project. They join group activities each week about research. They speak at a final symposium.
deadline_text: The page says applications for Summer 2027 open in December 2026. Close date not posted.

name: SFU Camps Volunteer
what_you_do: You help camp instructors run hands-on activities. The activities are for children and youth at SFU's Burnaby campus. You get leadership training. You write reflections. You go to career workshops.
deadline_text: 2026: online applications closed April 20, 2026 (Lead Volunteer deadline April 17, 2026); interviews mid-May (in person); training late June. 2027 dates are not posted.

name: H.R. MacMillan Space Centre teen volunteer
what_you_do: You volunteer at Vancouver's space science centre. You welcome visitors. You help set up headsets. You keep visitor flow smooth for the summer Augmented Reality Experience. You get education and skills training.
deadline_text: No dates are posted. The page refers to "this summer" without a year.

name: Stanley Park Ecology Youth Volunteering
what_you_do: You remove invasive plants. You host visitors at the Nature House. You can walk the park as an EcoRanger. You can also help at EcoCamp. Environmental educators give training.
deadline_text: Varies by role: DIRT and Nature House Host take applications year-round when there is room; EcoRangers apply in May; EcoCamp Assistant applications open in February and May; EcoStewards is listed as open.

name: UBC Future Global Leaders (on campus)
org: UBC Extended Learning, University of British Columbia
what_you_do: Take a university-style academic course or mini school taught by UBC professors and instructors on the Vancouver campus, with workshops and social activities. You get a letter of completion.
deadline_text: Summer 2027 sessions: July 5 to 16, July 19 to 30 and Aug 2 to 13, 2027. Residence registration deadlines (noon): May 21, June 4 and June 18, 2027. Commuter deadlines (noon): June 18, July 2 and July 16, 2027. Residence can close sooner if full. The page does not say when 2027 registration opens.

name: UBC Summer Science Program for Indigenous students
org: UBC Centre for Excellence in Indigenous Health, Faculty of Medicine
what_you_do: Spend one week on the UBC campus. You do cultural, health and science workshops. Examples are drum-making, a virtual reality medicine lab and Talking Circles led by Elders. You also meet Indigenous mentors in health and science.
deadline_text: The 2026 application deadline was June 15, 2026. The program page for 2025 listed Week 1 as Aug 3 to 9 and Week 2 as Aug 10 to 16, with applications closing June 1. 2027 dates are not posted.

name: Youth Explore Trades Sampler (Vancouver School Board)
what_you_do: Try several skilled trades in one semester. Try carpentry, electrical work, plumbing, iron work and sheet metal. Find the one that fits you.
deadline_text: Dates not stated on the program page. Ask your counsellor.

name: Youth WORK in Trades (Vancouver School Board)
org: Vancouver School Board Career Programs with SkilledTradesBC
what_you_do: Start a paid, part-time apprenticeship while in high school and earn up to 16 high school credits. Your job must be in a recognized trade.
deadline_text: The support form for finding a placement stays open until Dec 15 for semester 2 and May 15 for summer. Year not stated.

name: Vancouver Youth Parliament (VYP)
what_you_do: Debate real issues in a mock parliament over a weekend. Then join the fundraising and service events for the year.
deadline_text: The 39th session (Feb 6 to 8, 2026) closed applications Feb 1, 2026. The next one is expected around the same time.

name: VCC Dual Credit (high school trades and culinary foundation programs)
org: Vancouver Community College with Lower Mainland school districts
what_you_do: Take trades or cooking basics courses at VCC in your last years of high school. Examples are car repair, baking and hair styling.
deadline_text: No single deadline. Your school district career office sets the date.

name: Washington 4-H
what_you_do: Join a local 4-H club and pick one or more projects. Meet regularly. Clubs are led by elected youth officers. They take part in service learning, community outreach and other activities.
deadline_text: Enrollment opens on October 1 each year. The statewide Join page gives no closing date.

name: Washington Aerospace Scholars
city: Seattle, WA (online course, then a summer residency at the Museum of Flight)
what_you_do: This is a free online course on air and space vehicle design. It is a UW college course. It runs from November to March. Then there is an optional six-day summer residency. You design a Mars mission with industry mentors.
deadline_text: 2026-27 applications are open and close after October 13, 2026. Applicants are accepted on a rolling basis while room is available.

name: Washington DECA (high school)
org: Washington DECA, chartered association of DECA Inc.
what_you_do: Join your school's DECA chapter. You take a business or marketing class while in it. DECA supports local chapters. It runs a yearly state career development conference.
deadline_text: Membership deadlines come from your chapter advisor. The 2027 state conference is Feb 25 to 27, 2027 at the Meydenbauer Center in Bellevue.

name: Evergreen Boys & Girls State
what_you_do: Spend a week at Warm Beach Conference Center running a mock city, county and state government. You join a party, hold an office, run elections and make laws.
deadline_text: The page has Apply Now links for 2027 but does not say whether applications are open, and no deadline is posted. Spaces are limited each year, so apply early. The session is June 20 to 26, 2027. Check ebgs-wa.org before you plan on it.

name: Washington FFA Association
what_you_do: FFA is a student group tied to your school's farm and food class. Members build leadership and job skills at workshops, conferences and career events.
deadline_text: Join through your school's agriculture program.

name: Teen Volunteer Program
city: Bainbridge Island, Bremerton, Port Orchard, Poulsbo and Silverdale, WA
what_you_do: Volunteer at a library branch to build work-readiness skills. A library staff member contacts you after you apply.
deadline_text: No deadline stated.

name: Washington State Legislature Page Program (Senate and House)
what_you_do: Serve for one week at the State Capitol during the legislative session. You hand out materials and deliver messages. You carry the flags at the start of each day's session. You work on the chamber floor and attend Page School.
deadline_text: Applications for the 2027 session open Nov 1, 2026. No closing date is posted.

name: Sound to Summit Youth Crews
what_you_do: Work on a crew of teens with two adult leaders on park projects for four weeks. In week five you camp in a national park and do conservation work there.
deadline_text: 2026 sessions ran June 22 to July 24 and July 28 to Aug 28 (dates subject to change). 2027 dates and deadline not posted.

name: Youth Urban and Community Forestry Crew (Tacoma)
what_you_do: Join a crew of 8 teens and 2 adult leaders on tree and park projects in city parks, public lands and community gardens. About 32 hours a week of work plus 8 hours of training.
deadline_text: 2026 Washington sessions ran June 22 to July 24 and July 28 to Aug 28 (dates subject to change). 2027 dates and deadline not posted.

name: Running Start
org: Washington State Board for Community and Technical Colleges
what_you_do: 11th and 12th graders take college classes at a Washington community or technical college. They earn high school and college credit.
deadline_text: Deadlines are not stated on the SBCTC page; they vary by college.

name: Library Volunteering (all ages)
what_you_do: Help at your community library with a short project, a regular task or a special event. You go through an orientation and training and commit a regular part of your week.
deadline_text: The page does not post a deadline. Check with your local library for current openings.

name: Civil Air Patrol Cadet Program, Washington Wing
city: Statewide, WA (squadrons in Seattle, Yakima, Arlington and more)
what_you_do: Join a local squadron to learn leadership, aerospace, fitness and character. The Washington Wing lists a cadet competition and a cadet ball. It also lists an encampment. A ground search and rescue academy is listed too.
deadline_text: Join any time through a local squadron.

name: Youth Programs: Trail Work Parties
what_you_do: Youth build and fix hiking trails on one-day work parties and some multi-day trips, with trained crew leaders. Teams of youth can also book a private work party.
deadline_text: No deadline. Choose a work party any time (search the work party page).

name: Washington Youth ChalleNGe Academy
what_you_do: Live on campus in Bremerton for about five months in a free program for teens who have dropped out of high school or are at risk of it. You work on getting school credits back and on life skills.
deadline_text: Applications are open for the class that starts Jan 11, 2027. No closing date is posted. Spots go first come, first served.

name: YWCA NextStep
what_you_do: A free 12-week program with workshops, one-to-one support and a community project. You set goals and get real experience through volunteering, entry-level work or going back to school.
deadline_text: Registration is accepted on an ongoing basis. Upcoming cohorts: virtual Oct 13 and Oct 19, 2026; Port Coquitlam Oct 26, 2026; Prince George Jan 4, 2027; Langley and Kelowna Jan 11, 2027.
